findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed on their phone and donning gloves right after without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees stay off their phone and always wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer within the sani buckets were reading at 0ppm during the inspection. Education was carried out. A staff member remade the sani buckets and they tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer concentration are frequently checked to maintain appropriate sanitation of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed visible light beneath the door of the walk-in cooler. The gasket at the bottom of the door was observed broken. Ensure that this is repair allowing the walk-in cooler to be sealed properly.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: A staff member was observed not using a barrier after handwashing to shut off the faucet. Education was carried out. The staff member rewashed their hands following the appropriate procedures for drying their hands and shutting the faucet off. Ensure that a barrier is always use to shut off the facet after handwashing.

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Inspector observed raw chicken being stored above raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the raw chicken and stored it appropriately. Ensure that proper storage order is observed at all times to avoid cross contamination of food items. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed with a buildup of soil.
1. The internal dispensing surface of the ice cream machine was observed with an accumulation of soil.
2. The internal surface of the coffee machine was observed with a buildup of soil. 
3. A few cooking utensils (3 soup dippers) were observed rusted. PIC discarded them immediately. A sifter was observed soiled. 

The above mentioned food-contact surfaces were immediately cleaned to sight of touch. PIC discarded the rusted soup dippers as a corrective action. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at all times.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12  Inspector observed an accumulation of soil under the grill and the hot holding unit. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that these areas are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. This action will keep these areas free from the accumulation of food debris and soil. 

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil in the baffles of the ice machine. Discussed with PIC, who mentioned that the technician had just cleaned it the day before. PIC immediately discarded the ice in the ice machine and instructed the staff to start cleaning. The soil was removed, but some discoloration still stains the baffles. There is no further action needed for this violation. Ensure all food-contact areas on equipment are kept clean and sanitary.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed staff use the sanitizer wiping cloth to clean a surface then did not wash their hands before donning gloves for food prep. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are aware that they need to wash their hands whenever they change tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: An accumulation of soil was observed in the baffles of the ice machine. Discussed with PIC, who ensured inspectors that the the ice machine will be cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are routinely monitored and clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
The following cold holdings were observed in disrepair.
1. The freezer next to the fryer was observed to be in disrepair. 
2. The prep cooler opposite of the grill was observed in disrepair.
PIC was made aware and PIC called the maintenance technician while inspectors were present and the maintenance technician was scheduled to come by before the end of day to repair the equipment. Ensure that equipment for cold holding are routinely monitored to avoid food spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the plumbing line supplying the dish machine to be in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done in a timely manner. Ensure that plumbing lines such as the one supplying the dish machine are checked on a regular basis.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soil and food debris:
1. prep coolers adjacent to the grill
2. under the grill
3. under the prep coolers opposite the grill
4. under the countertop adjoining the register
5. under the dish machine and adjoining countertops
6. under the chili and mac & cheese reheating area

PIC was made aware that the above mentions area could benefit from a deep clean exercise. PIC ensured inspectors that the above mentioned areas will be cleaned. Ensure that spaces under equipment are routinely monitored and cleaned to avoid buildup.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be a bucket of pickles left uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC. PIC placed the lid back on the bucket of pickles. Ensure foods that are being stored are protected from-cross contamination at all times; in this case, placing a lid on the bucket is sufficient.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC had an employee start cleaning the microwave immediately. Ensure the microwave is kept clean to prevent cross-contamination between foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of food residues on the milkshake mixer arms and machine surface. Discussed with PIC. PIC had the machine cleaned immediately. Ensure all food-contact areas on equipment are kept clean and sanitary.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning. 

The hot holding in the back of the kitchen has an accumulation of soils on the machine surfaces. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the machine builds up hard-water soils as water evaporates on the machine. Ensure the machine is cleaned regularly to eliminate buildup of soils.

The corner of the dish line between the dish machine and the sink/sprayer combo was observed to have a large amount of soils. Discussed with PIC, recommended a cleaning regiment that includes that area as a frequently visited spot. Ensure that this area is cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.

Underneath the dish machine was observed to have a build up of soils. Discussed with PIC and recommended a cleaning regiment that includes the dish machine area as part of regular cleaning. Ensure this area is cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soils and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to still be an ice-buildup problem in the walk-in freezer. The lines have been repaired, as requested in the previous inspection. However, the buildup of ice persists to a lesser extent. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the machine is serviced to prevent this buildup of ice.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the following needs to be cleaned to protect food from cross contamination: (1) The entire inside of the microwave; (2) The fry buckets stored next to the fry scoop; and (3) Grease dripping over the cook line. Ensure that the inside of the microwave is cleaned to site and touch. Ensure that the fry scoop is not contaminating the fry buckets when putting the scoop back into the holder. Ensure that any drips coming from the hood over the cook line are cleaned. There will be a follow-up on 07/11/2024 to ensure these areas are cleaned. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer buckets were testing at 0 ppm - 100 ppm (Quat). The PIC was instructed to dump and re-fill the sanitizer buckets. After re-filling, the sanitizer buckets are testing at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are tested and changed at a frequency often enough to maintain proper concentrations (200 ppm for Quat).

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P)

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
